applies_to: PVI HeatStation boilers with the EOS BTCII touch-screen control, standalone or as the master of a cascade of up to 12 boilers, firmware J1239D-570 or newer.
summary: The boiler version of the PVI EOS BTCII control serves BACnet MS/TP (or Modbus RTU) from the master boiler's display. Besides boiler 1's probes, ignition state, modulation, relays, flame current, counters and error code, it gives the system (cascade) status, installed/talking/enabled boiler counts, the modulating and lead boiler, and writable system enable, BAS setpoint, setpoint and boiler enable. In a cascade the BAS connects only to the master.
notes: Object names and instances follow the discovery list printed in the manual. Only boiler 1 objects are printed; the manual says member boilers are numbered 2-12 but does not print their object instances.
Probes 4-6 and EMS VOLTAGE are only valid on boiler 1 (the master); probe 5 is the building supply / system sensor and probe 6 the outdoor sensor.
The point details list BOILER # DRIVE 2 at 1001 (pump 2, DHW/sanitary) and DRIVE 1 at 1002 (boiler pump), while the discovery list has DRIVE 1 at 1001 and DRIVE 2 at 1002. Check on site.
Flame current is reported with BACnet units of milliamperes, but the value is in tenths of a microamp (10 = 1 µA).

Error codes 1-31 (manual list): 1 EEPROM, 2 outdoor sensor, 3 supply sensor, 4 DHW sensor, 5 software, 6 FTBus comm, 7 LWCO, 8 remote proving, 9 air pressure, 10 low gas pressure, 11-14 outlet/inlet/vent/hi-limit sensor, 15 ignition failure, 16 flame loss, 17 vent hi-limit, 18 tank hi-limit, 19 false flame, 20 OEM card, 21 internal failure, 22 hi-delta, 23 low HSI, 24 low voltage, 25 blower speed, 26 high gas pressure, 27-31 linked-system communication.

source.title: EOS Boiler Interface Guide and Points List - For EOS BTCII Firmware Version J1239D-570 and Newer

integration.summary: Set the master boiler's BTCII network mode to BACnet, give it a device instance and MAC, and wire its 3-pin RS-485 terminal. Enable with SYSTEM ENABLE / BOILER 1 ENABLE, drive the temperature with BAS TARGET (or SETPOINT), and read SYSTEM STATUS, SYSTEM TEMP, the cascade counts, ALERT and ERROR.

minimum_points.name: BAS TARGET
minimum_points.why: BAS setpoint; overrides SETPOINT when non-zero

integration.enable: SYSTEM ENABLE (AV 0) and BOILER # ENABLE (AV 1000 for boiler 1) enable or disable with 1/0. The TH input (R1-R2, jumpered at the factory) must be closed; open on the master disables the whole system.
integration.remote_sensors: BAS TARGET (AV 1) takes over from SETPOINT whenever it is non-zero, until it is written back to 0 or the master loses power (it resets to 0 on power-up).
setup: On the display: Toolbox menu, access level ADV, then NETWORK menu: set MODE (BAS) to BACN.
Device instance is entered on the display (1-4194303); MAC 1-127 (default 3); baud 2400-115k (default 38k4); Max Master default 127; Max Info Frames default 1.
RS-485 on a 3-pin terminal on the back of the BTCII display: A(-) to the BAS D+, B(+) to D-, plus ground. No bias or termination resistors are built in.
The port is shared with Modbus RTU; only one protocol is active.
With the cascade feature in use, connect the BAS (or any gateway) to the master boiler only.
gotchas: BAS TARGET resets to 0 on a power cycle, so the boiler returns to SETPOINT; rewrite it after power-up.
SYSTEM STATUS does not show errors; a lockout reads as Idle.
